timeoutProcedure: Do not unplug the battery during the beeping
Push all the keys on the keypad
Make sure you have the correct combination

symptoms.label: Dial is stuck and will not move!
symptoms.recommendation: Stuck dial — do not force. Try dialing +/- 1-3 numbers off your combination. Call technician if no success.

symptoms.label: Dial is very sticky and/or tight to turn
symptoms.recommendation: Sticky dial — try compressed air around dial. If misaligned, tap lightly into place. Wheel pack issue needs new lock.

symptoms.label: Dial is loose, seems to spin too easy and will not engage to open
symptoms.recommendation: Dial loose from wear — try pulling dial toward you while dialing. If it opens, leave it open and call technician.

symptoms.label: Dialing the combination, it does not unlock easily and have to dial it multiple times
symptoms.recommendation: Dial not unlocking easily — try dialing slightly over/under target number. Wear will worsen over time.

symptoms.label: Lost or forgotten combination, probate, damaged in a burglary, or simply a broken dial lock
symptoms.recommendation: Lost combination or broken dial lock — technician required to open and repair.

symptoms.label: My keypad does not respond when I touch a key
symptoms.recommendation: Keypad unresponsive — check battery connections, cable to lock, and battery cartridge terminals.

symptoms.label: I put my combination in 3 times or more and now it beeps every 10 or 15 seconds
symptoms.recommendation: Lockout beeping — let stop, unplug battery, press all keys, plug back in, re-enter correct combination.

symptoms.label: Some of my keys do not register when I push them
symptoms.recommendation: Keys not registering — unplug battery, press all keys, replug and retry. Keypad may need replacement.

symptoms.label: I put in my combination, hear the solenoid click or motor turn, but the handle will not turn
symptoms.recommendation: Solenoid clicks but handle won't turn — move handle to neutral, try pushing toward lock and enter combo. Re-locker may have fired.

symptoms.label: I lost or forgot my combination
symptoms.recommendation: Lost electronic combination — technician needed. May be reset, shorted, or drilled depending on lock make.

symptoms.label: Handle is stuck and does not have any play
symptoms.recommendation: Stuck handle — push handle toward closed position, hold it, enter combo and try to open. Do not force.

symptoms.label: My handle moves or spins but it does not release the bolts to open the door
symptoms.recommendation: Handle spins but bolts don't release — check setscrew on handle hub. If tight, internal issue needs technician.

symptoms.label: My handle moves a little bit and I feel resistance when trying to open it
symptoms.recommendation: Handle has resistance — push on door while slowly moving handle to open. Stop if no progress.

symptoms.label: When opening the safe the door only comes open a little bit and stops
symptoms.recommendation: Door only opens partway — likely severed bolt connection. Call technician immediately. Do not force.

symptoms.label: I cannot lock my safe! I close it and throw the bolts but they will not lock in place
symptoms.recommendation: Cannot lock — check for obstruction blocking bolts. Open door 90°, release bolt detent, extend bolts fully.

symptoms.label: I don't have a heater or desiccant in my safe
symptoms.recommendation: Install reusable desiccant can or electric safe dryer to protect contents from moisture.

symptoms.label: I keep my safe in the garage, is that bad?
symptoms.recommendation: Garage safe — temperature extremes affect locks. Warm with hair dryer in winter, cool with fan in summer.

symptoms.label: I washed my keypad and it does not work right now
symptoms.recommendation: Keypad wet — let dry fully, use hair dryer on low from distance. If still fails, call technician.

symptoms.label: My safe is rusting at the bottom where it is anchored to the ground. Is that OK?
symptoms.recommendation: Bottom rust — create water barrier. Excessive rust compromises security. Replace and re-anchor ASAP.
